entities.name: PMID:25443761
observations: In 13 healthy lowlanders, high-intensity intermittent exercise increased lung-ultrasound B-lines at terrestrial 4090 m after acclimatization: 7 ± 4 at rest to 17 ± 5 immediately post-exercise, P < 0.001.
During acute normobaric hypoxia at FiO2 12% (approximately 4090-m equivalent), B-lines increased only 2 ± 2; values returned to baseline within 4 hours.
B-lines are an indirect marker consistent with pulmonary interstitial edema.

entities.name: PMID:34890833
observations: In 16 preterm-born young adults, 6 minutes of moderate exercise after 8 hours produced more lung-ultrasound B-lines at terrestrial 3840 m than under matched normobaric hypoxia: 4.6 ± 1.6 versus 3.1 ± 1.4, P = 0.0073.
This study is supportive of a hypobaric effect but does not directly test high-intensity intermittent exercise.

entities.name: HIIE altitude edema contrast
observations: A small human study found a clear post-exercise B-line increase at terrestrial altitude but only a small increase during acute simulated altitude.
The result supports, but does not definitively establish, greater exercise-related pulmonary interstitial edema at real altitude than simulated altitude.
